subject: Network dependency and latency SLO for private VPC (Kestrel Genomics)
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@kestrelgenomics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@kestrelgenomics.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification request — network dependency and latency SLO for Private VPC

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Kestrel is moving forward with the Private deployment in our AWS account, and procurement asked me to get a clear statement on how Redwood treats customer-managed network incidents with respect to latency and availability SLOs.

Our specific ask: can Redwood accept an addendum that explicitly states that any downtime or latency degradation caused by (a) customer-managed peering, transit, or egress issues; (b) customer firewall/NAT throttling; or (c) intermittent packet loss on the customer-controlled path will be excluded from Redwood's uptime and P99 latency calculations for the Private offering? We need this language for our security and procurement teams.

I've attached a simple topology diagram that shows our peering configuration. We plan to route inference traffic through the peering connection and will maintain our own egress gateways.

Attachment: kestrel-topology-diagram.pdf (pdf)

Could you provide suggested contract wording and confirm what telemetry Redwood needs from our side to validate incidents? Also: do you require any specific BGP or flow log retention settings?

Cheers,
Alice Chen
Director, Infrastructure
Kestrel Genomics

--
Alice Chen
Kestrel Genomics

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@kestrelgenomics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification request — network dependency and latency SLO for Private VPC

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear note and the diagram. Appreciate the context.

Short answer: yes, we can add a narrowly scoped carve-out to make clear that customer-controlled network failures are not counted against Redwood's P99 latency or availability SLOs, provided we have sufficient evidence to attribute the incident to the customer-managed path.

Proposed high-level contract language (draft):
"Redwood's uptime and latency Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for Private deployments apply to the Redwood-managed inference runtime and network segments under Redwood's operational control. Incidents primarily caused by customer-controlled networking components — including but not limited to peering, transit, customer egress gateways, firewall/NAT configurations, or other customer-managed network infrastructure — shall be excluded from Redwood's uptime and P99 latency measurements, provided Redwood can reasonably validate the cause using mutually agreed telemetry (BGP session state, NetFlow/flow logs, packet loss metrics, and Redwood call-stack traces)."

Telemetry we typically request for attribution: BGP session timestamps/RESET logs for the peering pair, VPC flow logs (retain for 30 days by default), cloud provider network status advisories, and any customer-side latency and packet-loss measurements during the event window. If Kestrel can produce flow logs and BGP state for the affected timeframe, our SREs can correlate with Redwood's ingress metrics to determine primary cause.

I've cc'd Vivek (runtime/I&O) and Monica (contracts) to review the wording and confirm whether we should add explicit retention windows or a maximum time-to-notify clause.

I'll attach a short draft addendum for your review.

Attachment: proposed-sla-addendum.docx (docx)

Best,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarification request — proposed carve-out language for Kestrel (see draft)

Folks — forwarding Kestrel's request and my draft addendum. High level: they want a clear carve-out for customer-managed network issues. I proposed the language below; legal/ops, please advise on two items we should confirm before sending to legal counterparty: 1) retention windows (I suggested 30 days for flow logs) and 2) an explicit "time-to-notify" requirement from the customer (I was thinking 48 hours after the incident start to ensure timely correlation).

Proposed wording (from my previous message):
"Incidents primarily caused by customer-controlled networking components — including but not limited to peering, transit, customer egress gateways, firewall/NAT configurations, or other customer-managed network infrastructure — shall be excluded from Redwood's uptime and P99 latency measurements, provided Redwood can reasonably validate the cause using mutually agreed telemetry (BGP session state, NetFlow/flow logs, packet loss metrics, and Redwood call-stack traces)."

Mina — can you surface any operational constraints we should call out (e.g., minimum sampling or agent instrumentation requirements) so we don't leave an attribution blind spot?

Monica — any concerns with the proposed notice period or the telemetry list? Do we need to add language around "good faith" cooperation for data sharing?

Thanks — want to get a vetted version back to Alice today.

— Dylan

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@kestrelgenomics.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@kestrelgenomics.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final proposed addendum and next steps (DocuSign)

Hi Alice — thanks for the patience. Monica and Vivek reviewed and we made two small edits: (1) we added a 48-hour customer notification requirement for incidents so Redwood can begin correlation work promptly; and (2) we explicitly call out a minimum 14-day retention for any packet-capture or debugging artifacts requested during an active investigation (flow logs remain 30 days as discussed).

Final suggested paragraph for the addendum:
"Redwood's uptime and P99 latency Service Level Objectives for Private deployments shall not apply to incidents where the preponderance of evidence indicates the primary cause resides in customer-managed networking components (including but not limited to peering, transit, customer egress gateways, or customer firewall/NAT devices). For an incident to be excluded, the customer must provide timely cooperation and sufficient telemetry to permit causal attribution, including but not limited to BGP session logs, VPC flow logs (minimum retention: 30 days), packet-capture or debugging artifacts upon request (minimum retention during investigation: 14 days), and customer-side latency/packet-loss measurements. The customer agrees to notify Redwood within 48 hours of incident onset unless prevented by demonstrable constraints. Redwood will use these data to determine whether the incident is excluded from uptime and latency calculations."

I sent the addendum to DocuSign for signature and included our standard monitoring checklist in the Drive link below. Please review the addendum and the monitoring checklist and let me know if anything else is needed from your side before signature.
